clue.text: Incentive for proposal introducing international tax

indicators.note: the proposal takes the following letters into its middle, as if bringing them inside

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A political proposal that brings in an international levy as a spur to action.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the UK's value added tax, a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a motivation is what drives or spurs someone, just as an incentive does.

clue.text: Described car as dark

indicators.note: something described is put into spoken words, so the car's short name is heard rather than written

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes car

explanation.surface: Someone recounting what their car looked like: dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merc' is short for a Mercedes; said out loud it matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: murk is gloom or darkness, so it matches dark used as a noun.

clue.text: A lot to expect of high command

parts.note: tall means high
an order is a command

explanation.surface: Orders from the top brass demand a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a demanding request that is hard to fulfil is called this phrase.

clue.text: Poem is not about defeat

indicators.note: 'is not' says the following word for about is missing from the word for defeat

parts.note: a reverse is a defeat or setback
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A poem that refuses to dwell on failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: verse is poetry, and a single poem can be called a verse.

clue.text: Wrong to imprison those of one sex for harassment

indicators.note: the word for wrong locks the people inside it, as a jail holds prisoners

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are those of one sex

explanation.surface: It is wrong to lock up all of one gender as a form of persecution.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: torment is persistent distressing persecution, much like harassment.

clue.text: Times journalist goes after award I failed

indicators.note: the journalist's letters come after the rest, following on behind

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British award
T for time, twice over for the plural
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer chases a prize the speaker missed out on.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense of neglect: something omitted is something one failed to include or do.

clue.text: I returned last month chilled to the bone

indicators.note: the abbreviation of the month is turned back to read right to left

parts.note: December, the last month of the year, is DEC

explanation.surface: Someone back from a December trip, frozen through.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: iced means frozen or thoroughly chilled.

clue.text: King to succeed Charlie? It's obvious

indicators.note: succeed means come after, so the king follows the letter

parts.note: C is Charlie in the phonetic alphabet
Lear is Shakespeare's king

explanation.surface: A royal succession question: the King following Charles seems self-evident.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests King Charles's heir; 'King' is really Lear, and Charlie only the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: clear and obvious both mean plain to see.

clue.text: Planned to berate idle drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A scheme to scold a lazy person who is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something deliberate is intended or done on purpose, i.e. planned.

clue.text: Gladly accepts that we'll mostly arrive by bus in the end

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: the contraction without its apostrophe is WELL
to come is to arrive

indicators.note: take only the final letter of the word for the vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone happily confirming that they will get there by bus eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to welcome something is to receive it gladly.

clue.text: Person in charge of government measure

definitions.meaning: a sovereign or leader who governs a country
a straight-edged strip for measuring length

explanation.surface: A leader in charge of a government policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a monarch who governs, and a graduated strip used to measure.

clue.text: Her allies unexpectedly make a lot of trouble

indicators.note: the letters turn up in a surprising new arrangement

explanation.surface: Her friends cause an unexpected uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to kick up a fuss or cause uproar is to make a lot of trouble.

clue.text: Understandable being firm at this point with conservationists

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
here means at this point
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity

explanation.surface: A company's position on conservation groups is easy to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a coherent argument is logical and clear, therefore understandable.

clue.text: Like chocolate bar blended with 40% cocoa

indicators.note: blended suggests ingredients mixed up into a new order
two of the five letters is forty percent, taken from the start

explanation.surface: A chocolate bar made with forty percent cocoa solids.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of a substitute: carob is a pod product used as a chocolate-like alternative.

clue.text: Disgusting that an explosive device is reported in Aberfoyle's suburbs

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the device's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: a bomb is an explosive device
taken as written

indicators.note: suburbs are the outskirts, so keep the outer letters and lose the centre

parts.note: Aberfoyle is a village in Scotland; its two letters at each end are kept

explanation.surface: A news report of a bomb on the edge of a Scottish village, condemned as appalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is reported' makes 'a bomb' sound as ABOM; 'suburbs' keeps the outer pairs AB and LE of Aberfoyle, a Scottish village.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: abominable means loathsome or detestable, i.e. disgusting.

clue.text: Enforced idleness in middle of the day trapped in French port

indicators.note: the picked letters are held inside the port's name

parts.note: Brest is a port in Brittany

indicators.note: the central two letters of the words 'the day'

explanation.surface: Stuck in a French harbour at midday with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of the day' is literal: the middle letters of THE DAY are ED, not noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical rest: a doctor orders it, so idleness is enforced while staying lying down.

clue.text: Mushroom escalope more than half consumed

indicators.note: five of the eight letters of the word, from the start, is more than half

parts.note: ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A mushroom escalope, most of it already eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' is a verb here, meaning grow rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to mushroom is to grow fast, as things that escalate do.

clue.text: Objector drops resistance and becomes more modest

indicators.note: the objector loses the letter for resistance

parts.note: a demurrer is one who demurs, or objects
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An objector stops resisting and turns meek.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative: demure means modest and reserved, so this form means more modest.

clue.text: Delighted to criticise America over shambolic rout

indicators.note: the country's letters sit at the end of this down entry, beyond the rest

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply

indicators.note: shambolic means chaotic, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: Pleased to slam the US after a chaotic defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rapturous means filled with great joy, i.e. delighted.

clue.text: Wonder at the Spanish vehicle reversing on motorway

indicators.note: in an across entry, on means placed after the motorway

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI

indicators.note: the pair of pieces read backwards, like a car backing up

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Marvelling at a Spanish car backing up on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a miracle is a marvel, a wonder.

clue.text: Wind up more ill without a wife to give support

parts.note: to end is to wind up

indicators.note: the word for sicker goes without the letter for a wife

parts.note: worse means more ill
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Ending up sicker, with no spouse to lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to endorse is to back or approve, giving support.

clue.text: Stickler about full stops left out altogether

indicators.note: about here means moved around, mixing the letters
every one of the letters for left is cut out

parts.note: L is left; both of them go

explanation.surface: A pedant fussing about full stops being omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out altogether' removes both Ls from FULL STOPS, leaving FUSTOPS, which 'about' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stickler is a person who is fussy about details.

clue.text: Father's collapse

definitions.meaning: the father of an enterprise is the person who set it up
to collapse or sink, as a ship or a plan

explanation.surface: A dad's breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the originator who established something, and to fail or sink.

clue.text: Book would get a prize if central character were changed

indicators.note: the middle letter of the prize's name is swapped for another

parts.note: the Nobel is a prize

explanation.surface: A book that would win a prize if its protagonist were rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central character' sounds like a protagonist but means the middle letter: Nobel's B becomes V.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a novel is a long fictional book.

clue.text: Unionist engaged in heartless empty boast

indicators.note: the letter is set into the trimmed word
the word for empty loses its central letters

parts.note: vacant means empty

explanation.surface: A union man involved in hollow bragging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes CA from the middle of VACANT, leaving VANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to vaunt is to brag about something, i.e. boast.

clue.text: Party turn initially booked through friends unfortunately looks uncertain

parts.note: a do is a party
U as in a U-turn

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A party act booked through friends looks shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: doubtful means not sure, uncertain.

clue.text: A hint of tense competition

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a contest is getting tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a trace is a very small amount or slight sign, a hint.

clue.text: Sentry guarding crowded conference ends up irritable

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
take the last letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A guard at a packed conference becomes tetchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: edgy means tense and nervy, easily irritated.

clue.text: "Be without covetousness!" leftie ranted

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word wraps around the desire

parts.note: lust is strong desire or covetousness
a Red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: A left-winger angrily preaching against greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bluster is to speak loudly and aggressively, as one who rants.

clue.text: Shun old and extremely ill- conceived electoral system at first

indicators.note: the voting system's letters go at the front

parts.note: AV is the alternative vote

indicators.note: take the outer letters, at the extremes

explanation.surface: A call to reject an outdated and badly thought-out voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: AV, the alternative vote, was a voting system rejected in a 2011 UK referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to avoid someone is to keep away from them, shun them.

clue.text: Takes in inside knowledge at school

indicators.note: the letters are found running inside these words

explanation.surface: A pupil absorbing insider knowledge at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: eats means consumes, takes in food.

clue.text: Woman with no means of hearing regularly plays without anxiety

parts.note: F is short for female
earless means without ears

indicators.note: take every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A deaf woman performing music with complete calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: acting fearlessly means acting without fear or worry.
